items.question: Why does the node2vec method rely on global graph statistics and offline processing to learn its latent social representations?
items.false_premise: node2vec relies on global graph statistics and offline processing.
items.correction: node2vec proposes a scalable online method which uses only local information.
items.evidence_quote: We propose a scalable online method which uses only local information.

items.question: How does node2vec extend the collective classification procedure itself with graph kernels to improve inference?
items.false_premise: node2vec extends the collective classification procedure itself with graph kernels.
items.correction: node2vec does not attempt to extend the classification procedure itself, and instead learns representations that can be used by existing inference procedures.
items.evidence_quote: We do not attempt to extend the classification procedure itself (through collective inference [37] or graph kernels [20]).

items.question: Under which conditions does node2vec need many random walks per vertex before its embeddings become meaningful?
items.false_premise: node2vec needs many random walks per vertex before its embeddings become meaningful.
items.correction: node2vec can learn meaningful latent representations after only a small number of random walks, and increasing the number of walks quickly has diminishing returns.
items.evidence_quote: These results demonstrate that we are able to learn meaningful latent representations for vertices after only a small number of random walks.

items.question: What centrality-based statistics does node2vec compute instead of learning latent social representations?
items.false_premise: node2vec computes centrality-based statistics instead of learning latent social representations.
items.correction: node2vec learns latent social representations rather than computing statistics related to centrality or partitioning.
items.evidence_quote: We learn our latent social representations, instead of computing statistics related to centrality [12] or partitioning [41].
